summary: Iteration 2 testing complete. Backend: 9/9 pytest cases pass covering the two new endpoints and the artistHandle regression. Frontend (390x844 mobile web): Artist page (via player-artist-link and via action-view-artist) loads correctly with name/verified badge/followers/track count/bio/top tracks; artist-play and artist-shuffle both trigger playback; top-track row plays a track. Playlist Detail: created a playlist from player-more -> action-create-playlist, opened it from Library > Playlists tab, playlist-play and playlist-shuffle both work; playlist-edit-toggle switches into edit mode; remove-track fires the correct API + shows 'Removed from playlist' toast + updates count. Reorder (move-down/move-up) exercised in-UI on a single-track playlist (see caveat) and independently verified at the API layer with a 3-track playlist. No deprecated Expo packages (expo-av/expo-barcode-scanner/expo-background-fetch). No SafeAreaView issues detected.

issues: React Native Web 'shadow*' style prop deprecation warnings still logged in console (pre-existing, cosmetic).

critical_code_review_comments: GET /api/artists/{handle} correctly proxies Audius /users/handle and /users/{id}/tracks, normalizes cover/image/isVerified/followerCount/trackCount, and returns 404 for unknown handles.
PUT /api/library/playlist/{id}/reorder uses a stable index-map sort (unknown ids sink to 9999) so the endpoint is order-preserving; returns 404 for unknown playlist ids.
TrackPayload now includes optional artistHandle; slim() on the frontend passes artistHandle so the artist-jump feature keeps working across favorite/recent/playlist add.
playlist/[id].tsx keeps a local `order` state and syncs from library; reorderMutation is fired eagerly after local swap (optimistic UI). Remove is also optimistic then invalidated.
artist page hero uses cover/image fallback + gradient; back button uses hitSlop=12 and top offset from insets — good.
seed_data_creation: device_id='test_device_2' library: created 'TEST_Reorder_PL' with 3 seed tracks (added/reordered/cleaned up by pytest). UI created 'TEST_PL_iter2c' on the default device (with one track then removed).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reuse /app/backend/tests/test_iteration2.py and /app/backend/tests/test_liquidaudio.py. Tab bar uses default Expo Router tab labels (no tab-<name> testIDs) — click by visible text ('Home','Search','Sound','Library') via get_by_text. Library segment is [data-testid=library-tab-Playlists]. Playlist row uses testID=playlist-<uuid> (match /^playlist-[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-/). track-row-<id> and track-more-<id> may appear in more than one place (mini-player + list); filter to unique ids before clicking to avoid strict-mode ambiguity. Playlist detail reorder is best exercised on a playlist with >=3 tracks; adding tracks in UI requires scrolling and using unique track-more testIDs.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no functional bugs found. During UI reorder verification, only one extra track ended up in the newly-created playlist (the UI 'add-to-playlist' iteration reused the same track index), so the in-UI move-down/move-up sequence was exercised with a shorter list than intended. The reorder endpoint itself is fully verified via test_iteration2.py::TestPlaylistReorder with 3 tracks in two orderings, and the frontend calls reorderPlaylist(...) with the correctly-permuted id list. Recommend the main agent (optional) do a manual sanity swap in a 3-track playlist to visually confirm the arrow reorder animation.
